markers.label: Luang Namtha
markers.description: Luang Namtha marks the northern Lao town whose fall exposed Royal Lao weakness early in the civil war.

slides.title: From Vietnam War to Laotian Civil War
slides.body: The Vietnam War spread beyond Vietnam because both sides depended on neighboring territory. North Vietnam used routes through Laos to move troops and supplies, while the United States supported anti-communist forces and conducted a covert air campaign. Laos became an inseparable battlefield of the wider war.

stats.lbl: The Vietnam War spread beyond Vietnam because both sides depended on neighboring territory. slides.title: Battle of Luang Namtha
slides.body: The Battle of Luang Namtha, fought between January 1962 and May 1963, was a series of clashes in the Laotian Civil War. It came about as a result of the turmoil following Laotian independence as a result of the First Indochina War with France. The Kingdom of Laos had foreign soldiers on its soil, and a political struggle in progress concerning those outside troops. Following a coup and counter-coup that left General Phoumi Nosavan in charge, the general decided on military action to settle the political issue of interlopers in Laos. For the United States, Luang Namtha highlighted the weakness of Royal Lao forces and the difficulty of containing Pathet Lao advances.

stats.lbl: It pushed Washington toward deeper covert involvement rather than open conventional war.

slides.title: The Wider Impact

markers.label: Lak Sao
markers.description: Lak Sao marks the central Lao crossroads where Royal Lao forces fought North Vietnamese and Pathet Lao troops.

slides.title: Battle of Lak Sao
slides.body: The Battle of Lak Sao, fought between November 1963 and January 1964, was a major engagement of the Laotian Civil War. In November 1963, General Phoumi Nosavan, who held the reins of military power in the Kingdom of Laos, launched a military offensive against North Vietnamese invaders that cut across the northern panhandle of the nation. Although unsupported in this proxy action by his backers in the U.S. Embassy, he went ahead with his plan to push northwards from Nhommarath, then veer eastwards to the Vietnamese border. Phoumi's Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) advisors warned him that the North Vietnamese would retaliate, but he disregarded them. Lak Sao showed how difficult it was for US-backed forces to hold remote ground against coordinated communist pressure.

stats.lbl: It reinforced the limits of proxy warfare in Laos.

slides.title: The Wider Impact
slides.body: It reinforced the limits of proxy warfare in Laos.

markers.label: Ban Khwan
markers.description: Ban Khwan marks the northwestern Lao battlefield where rival opium forces and Royal Lao troops clashed in 1967.

markers.label: Ban Houayxay
markers.description: Ban Houayxay marks the nearby Mekong base area involved in the Opium War fighting.

slides.title: 1967 Opium War
slides.body: The 1967 Opium War took place in northwestern Laos between February and August 1967; actual fighting took place from 29 July to 1 August 1967. A mule train, led by Burmese militia, carrying 16 tons of opium crossed into Laos to Ban Khwan, where they were attacked by rival drug smugglers from the Chinese Nationalists' Third and Fifth Armies. The intended recipient of the shipment, Royal Lao Army General Ouane Rattikone, bombed both sides while moving in troops to sweep the battlefield. With both Burmese militia and Kuomintang (KMT) Army defeated and expelled from Laos, the Lao general confiscated the opium for himself. The Opium War revealed how local power, narcotics, militias, and intelligence networks overlapped in the Laotian conflict.

stats.lbl: It exposed the messy local realities behind America's anti-communist strategy.

slides.title: The Wider Impact

markers.label: Nam Bac Valley
markers.description: Nam Bac Valley marks the Royal Lao stronghold whose collapse became a major communist victory.

slides.title: Battle of Nam Bac
slides.body:
The Battle of Nam Bac was one of the major engagements of the Laotian Civil War. Despite misgivings about their potential performance the Royal Lao Army moved in to occupy the Nam Bac Valley in August 1966; the position would block a traditional Vietnamese invasion route that led to the Lao royal capitol, Luang Prabang. Nam Bac was a major defeat for Royal Lao forces despite US support and air power.

It showed that air support could not compensate for fragile local command and morale.

stats.lbl: It showed that air support could not compensate for fragile local command and morale.

markers.label: Xieng Lom
markers.description: Xieng Lom marks the Mekong border area where Thai-backed forces established a forward defensive position in Laos.

markers.label: Pakbeng
markers.description: Pakbeng marks the Mekong corridor and Chinese road concern behind Thai intervention planning.

slides.title: Operation Phalat
slides.body:
Operation Phalat was a military offensive of the Laotian Civil War aimed at an active defense of the Kingdom of Thailand's northern border with the Kingdom of Laos. Evoked by the approach of The Chinese Road, and despite feeble cooperation from the Royal Lao Government, the Thai military established a three-battalion presence on Lao territory south of the Mekong River as a defense against potential invasion by the People's Republic of China. Operation Phalat reflected the continuing attempt to use local and regional forces to contest communist control without admitting a full US war.

It illustrates the hidden-war logic of Laos.

stats.lbl: It illustrates the hidden-war logic of Laos.

markers.label: Xieng Lom
markers.description: Xieng Lom marks the Mekong sector around which Operation Sourisak Montry VIII unfolded.

markers.label: Pakbeng
markers.description: Pakbeng marks the nearby Mekong crossing area tied to the Chinese road and Thai security fears.

slides.title: Operation Sourisak Montry VIII
slides.body:
Operation Sourisak Montry VIII was a Thai military offensive against an encroaching Chinese Communist presence just north of the Mekong River. Operation Phalat established a base camp at Xieng Lom, Laos, on the southern bank of the Mekong River, and garrisoned it with three Thai mercenary battalions. Operation Sourisak Montry was a series of indecisive skirmishes in the same area, during which the Thais won a Pyrrhic victory over the Pathet Lao in mid-March 1972. This operation was part of the repeated effort to shift local front lines through limited offensives and proxy forces.

It shows the war's grinding character and the difficulty of producing lasting results.

stats.lbl: It shows the war's grinding character and the difficulty of producing lasting results.

markers.label: Vientiane
markers.description: Vientiane marks the treaty negotiations that produced the 1973 coalition settlement.

slides.title: Vientiane Treaty
slides.body:
The Vientiane Treaty was a cease-fire agreement between the two warring factions in the Laotian Civil War, signed in Vientiane, on 21 February 1973. For Washington, the Vientiane settlement offered a political way to reduce pressure while preserving some anti-communist influence.

It marked the attempt to turn an unwinnable covert battlefield into a negotiated balance.

stats.lbl: It marked the attempt to turn an unwinnable covert battlefield into a negotiated balance.

markers.label: Vientiane
markers.description: Vientiane marks the political center of the 1973 coup attempt and postwar instability.

slides.title: 1973 Laotian coup
slides.cap: The end and legacy of the Laotian Civil War
slides.body: The 1973 Laotian coup d'état attempt was a final attempt to stave off a communist coalition government of the Kingdom of Laos. Exiled General Thao Ma returned from the Kingdom of Thailand on 20 August 1973 to take over Wattay International Airport outside the capital of Vientiane. Commandeering an AT-28, he led air strikes upon the office and home of his hated rival, General Kouprasith Abhay. While Thao Ma was unsuccessfully bombing Kouprasith, loyal Royalist troops retook the airfield. Shot down upon his return, Thao Ma was hauled from his airplane's wreckage and executed. The coalition agreement was signed 14 September 1973. The coup reflected the instability of Laos even as the wider Vietnam War was winding down.

stats.lbl: It showed that American withdrawal did not immediately create political stability in the region.

slides.cap: The end and legacy of the Laotian Civil War

slides.title: War Summary: Laotian Civil War
slides.cap: The end and legacy of the Laotian Civil War
slides.body: The communist Pathet Lao took power in 1975 as the wider Indochina wars ended. Laos emerged deeply scarred by displacement, unexploded ordnance, and years of covert warfare.
